item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00030","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C20","C17","C09"],"selected_candidate_label":"C20","confidence":0.97,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C20 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both memoranda reject a direct private award because the underlying evidence is disputed and ordinary procedural requirements were not met, yet conclude that fairness warrants legislation waiving the limitations barrier so the claim can be adjudicated on its merits through established procedures. This distinctive rejection-plus-alternative-remedy sequence is materially closer than the general objections to individualized veterans relief in C17 or the jurisdictional legislation discussed in C09.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The evidence in this case is complex and controversial. I believe, therefore, that in fairness to Mrs. McQuilkin she is entitled to a day in court for decision of her claim on its merits","parent_excerpt":"There is conflicting evidence regarding the facts in this case... I believe that the claimant should be afforded the opportunity to advance any additional evidence he may have in support of his claim.","explanation":"Both pivot from evidentiary uncertainty to allowing a formal merits determination."},{"child_excerpt":"I would be willing to approve a jurisdictional enactment waiving the bar of any statute of limitations.","parent_excerpt":"I would, therefore, be willing to approve a bill which would permit a determination of the claimant's employment status... and which would then permit him, notwithstanding any statute of limitations, to file a claim under the law applicable to that status.","explanation":"The proposed substitute remedy is nearly identical: reject the direct award but endorse legislation overcoming the limitations bar."},{"child_excerpt":"I also agree with the Veterans' Administration that the case does not present any equitable consideration which warrants the direct gratuity award proposed.","parent_excerpt":"I find no justification for this proposed award... It constitutes a method of payment which is at variance with the periodic compensation benefits provided by existing law.","explanation":"Both reject an immediate lump-sum private award in favor of adjudication under regular legal procedures."}]}
